# Overview

> InoQuill v1.0.0 by TabGrinder

A quick introduction and a guide to your first conversion.

InoQuill helps you turn Arduino keyboard sketches into DuckyScript for your device. Everything runs in your browser. Start with an example or your own sketch, then check the result before downloading it.

InoQuill is free to use, modify, and share under the MIT license.

## Three steps from sketch to script

- Add a sketch: paste your code, choose a file, or try an example.
- Convert and review: choose your device, select Convert sketch, and read the output and any notices.
- Download your script: use the instructions for your device to prepare and test it.

> A successful conversion means InoQuill could translate the operations in your sketch. You still need to review the script, compile it if your device requires that, and test it with the right keyboard layout.

## What to look for

- If InoQuill cannot determine what an operation does, it asks you to review it before exporting.
- Source trace connects each output instruction to the line in your sketch.
- Download a review report to keep the selected settings, diagnostic messages, and delay totals.
- Conversion runs separately from the interface, with limits on processing time and output size. InoQuill does not run or upload your sketch.

Visit Project to learn about InoQuill and the tools that inspired it. The guides here cover conversion, device setup, and troubleshooting.
